share.who: an engineer who mixes up their reverse proxy, load balancer and API gateway
share.why: a three-question rule of thumb: which server is healthy, who is calling, which path goes where

replay.twist: On a second watch the hook 'Your 1 proxy_pass can be a reverse proxy, but also a load balancer' reads as the lesson: proxy_pass at 1 server is a reverse proxy, at an upstream group of 3 it is a load balancer, and the gateway adds who is calling.

length_reason: About 105 s on purpose: a COMPARE deep dive where each of the 3 jobs needs its own real artefact (proxy_pass, upstream group with max_fails and fail_timeout defaults, ALB health check defaults and its only-unhealthy-targets behaviour, API Gateway authorization, auth_request and limit_req).

claims.say: In NGINX a reverse proxy uses a location block with proxy_pass (example shape: location, proxy_pass to one server).
claims.quote: location /some/path/ {

claims.say: The docs example passes the request with proxy_pass inside a location block.
claims.quote: proxy_pass http://www.example.com/link/;

claims.say: proxy_pass passes all requests processed in that location to the proxied server.
claims.quote: This example configuration results in passing all requests processed in this location to the proxied server at the specified address.

claims.say: Proxying distributes the load among several servers (reverse proxy and load balancer roles overlap).
claims.quote: Proxying is typically used to distribute the load among several servers

claims.say: proxy_pass can point to a named group of servers, so the same directive serves a load balancer.
claims.quote: The proxy_pass directive can also be used to pass requests to a named group of servers

claims.say: A reverse proxy can also do load balancing (roles overlap).
claims.quote: Load balancing: distribute the load to several web servers,

claims.say: Example upstream group of 3 servers: upstream myapp1 { ... }
claims.quote: upstream myapp1 {

claims.say: Group member srv1.example.com.
claims.quote: server srv1.example.com;

claims.say: Group member srv2.example.com.
claims.quote: server srv2.example.com;

claims.say: Group member srv3.example.com.
claims.quote: server srv3.example.com;

claims.say: proxy_pass points at the upstream group.
claims.quote: proxy_pass http://myapp1;

claims.say: nginx applies HTTP load balancing to the server group.
claims.quote: All requests are proxied to the server group myapp1, and nginx applies HTTP load balancing to distribute the requests.

claims.say: With no method configured, it defaults to round-robin.
claims.quote: When the load balancing method is not specifically configured, it defaults to round-robin.

claims.say: A failing server is marked failed and nginx tries to avoid it for a while.
claims.quote: If the response from a particular server fails with an error, nginx will mark this server as failed, and will try to avoid selecting this server for subsequent inbound requests for a while.

claims.say: max_fails defaults to 1.
claims.quote: By default, the number of unsuccessful attempts is set to 1.

claims.say: fail_timeout defaults to 10 seconds.
claims.quote: By default, the parameter is set to 10 seconds.

claims.say: fail_timeout is the period the server is considered unavailable.
claims.quote: the period of time the server will be considered unavailable.

claims.say: An AWS Application Load Balancer monitors target health and routes only to healthy targets.
claims.quote: It monitors the health of its registered targets, and routes traffic only to the healthy targets.

claims.say: ALB health check interval defaults to 30 seconds (instance or ip targets).
claims.quote: The default is 30 seconds if the target type is `instance` or `ip`

claims.say: HealthCheckIntervalSeconds setting name.
claims.quote: HealthCheckIntervalSeconds

claims.say: UnhealthyThresholdCount setting name.
claims.quote: UnhealthyThresholdCount

claims.say: ALB unhealthy threshold count defaults to 2.
claims.quote: The range is 2–10. The default is 2.

claims.say: If a target group contains only unhealthy targets, the load balancer routes requests to all of them.
claims.quote: If a target group contains only unhealthy registered targets, the load balancer routes requests to all those targets

claims.say: Amazon API Gateway tasks: traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, API version management.
claims.quote: These tasks include traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, and API version management.

claims.say: auth_request implements client authorization based on a subrequest.
claims.quote: implements client authorization based on the result of a subrequest.

claims.say: auth_request allows on 2xx.
claims.quote: If the subrequest returns a 2xx response code, the access is allowed.

claims.say: auth_request denies on 401 or 403.
claims.quote: If it returns 401 or 403, the access is denied with the corresponding error code.

claims.say: auth_request /auth; config line.
claims.quote: auth_request /auth;

claims.say: limit_req_zone with rate=1r/s config line (an NGINX example of rate limiting; not a claim about the Amazon API Gateway list).
claims.quote: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=1r/s;

claims.say: limit_req with burst=5 config line.
claims.quote: limit_req zone=one burst=5;

claims.say: Rejected requests get status 503 by default.
claims.quote: Default: limit_req_status 503;

claims.say: limit_req_status sets the status code for rejected requests.
claims.quote: Sets the status code to return in response to rejected requests.

claims.say: Decision rule: load balancer asks which server is healthy (monitors health of targets).
claims.quote: It monitors the health of its registered targets, and routes traffic only to the healthy targets.

claims.say: Decision rule: API gateway handles authorization and access control.
claims.quote: These tasks include traffic management, authorization and access control, monitoring, and API version management.

claims.say: Decision rule: reverse proxy sends a path's requests to the proxied server.
claims.quote: This example configuration results in passing all requests processed in this location to the proxied server at the specified address.

claims.say: Side note: with a single server in a group, max_fails and fail_timeout are ignored.
claims.quote: If there is only a single server in a group, max_fails, fail_timeout and slow_start parameters are ignored,

claims.say: A single server is never considered unavailable.
claims.quote: and such a server will never be considered unavailable.

claims.say: max_fails sets the number of unsuccessful attempts to communicate with the server.
claims.quote: sets the number of unsuccessful attempts to communicate with the server

claims.say: The attempts are counted in the duration set by fail_timeout.
claims.quote: that should happen in the duration set by the fail_timeout parameter

claims.say: ALB health checks run at an interval (approximate time between checks).
claims.quote: The approximate amount of time, in seconds, between health checks of an individual target.

claims.say: UnhealthyThresholdCount: number of consecutive failed health checks before a target is unhealthy.
claims.quote: The number of consecutive failed health checks required before considering a target unhealthy.

claims.quote: the load balancer routes requests to all those targets, regardless of their health status.
